source_reachability:
All statuses observed by me with curl -A "Mokaair-editorial" on 2026-09-16.

RECORDED SOURCES:

2. https://www.enisa.europa.eu/news/the-cra-single-reporting-platform-is-launched -> HTTP 200, 49,815 bytes, real content, labelled "Press Release / Sep 11,2026".
3. https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/product-security/single-reporting-platform-srp/frequently-asked-questions -> HTTP 200, 78,755 bytes, 31 numbered FAQs, "Updated: 12 September 2026".
4. https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R2847 -> CONDITIONAL, and the researcher's recipe does not reproduce. With NO Accept-Language header every Accept type returns HTTP 400 with a 205-byte error body (tested twice). Only with "Accept-Language: eng" added: application/xhtml+xml -> 200, 710,696 bytes, full OJ text (cellar 21b7d4eb-a6e2-11ef-85f0-01aa75ed71a1.0006.03/DOC_1, title L_202402847EN.000101.fmx.xml); text/html -> 404; application/pdf -> 404. A browser-style Accept -> 200 but serves application/rdf+xml, 2,001,488 bytes: metadata, NOT the Regulation.

10. https://www.enisa.europa.eu/topics/product-security-and-certification/single-reporting-platform-srp -> HTTP 200 only after redirect to /topics/product-security/... The researcher's stale-URL correction is confirmed.

NOT FETCHED BY ME OR THE RESEARCHER: https://portal.cra-srp.enisa.europa.eu (EU Login wall). Correctly recorded as "ENISA publishes this address" only.

NEW, WORKING, FIRST-PARTY, MISSED BY THE RESEARCHER: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary -> HTTP 200, 123,150 bytes, "Last update 3 December 2025". See refuted and additional_findings.

refuted.fact: unverified_or_excluded entry 4: "The CRA entered into force on 10 December 2024 ... No official page I reached states an exact entry-into-force date, and I am not going to publish a date I calculated myself."
refuted.why: REFUTED. The Commission's own "Cyber Resilience Act - Summary of the legal text" page states it verbatim: "The CRA entered into force on 10 December 2024. It will be fully applicable as of 11 December 2027 with some provisions starting to apply earlier: Chapter IV on the notification of conformity assessment bodies will apply from 11 June 2026, whereas reporting obligations set out in Article 14 apply from 11 September 2026." I fetched https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary, HTTP 200, 123,150 bytes, Last update 3 December 2025. That page is the "Cyber Resilience Act - Summary of the legal text" Quick Link ON the cra-reporting page already in sources, so it was one click away. The caution was methodologically right but the premise was wrong: the date does not have to be calculated, and it is available first-party.

refuted.fact: sourcing_notes: "https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R2847 returns HTTP 404 for 'Accept: text/html' and for 'Accept: application/pdf', but HTTP 200 for 'Accept: application/xhtml+xml'."
refuted.why: REFUTED as a reproduction recipe. Following it verbatim I got HTTP 400 with a 205-byte error body for ALL THREE Accept types, on two separate runs. The undocumented requirement is an Accept-Language header: only with "Accept-Language: eng" do the stated 404/404/200 results appear. Anyone re-verifying this source by the recorded recipe will conclude it is dead. The researcher must have sent Accept-Language and not written it down.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[54], the sub-claims "Section 9.1 of that guidance covers reporting obligations" and "The Commission also publishes 'FAQs on the CRA implementation', Section 5 of which covers reporting."
unsupported.why: Not present on the attached URL. I fetched the guidance-announcement page (HTTP 200) and grepped the extracted text: 0 occurrences of "9.1", 0 occurrences of "Section 5". The rest of fact [54] (67 practical examples, non-binding, in force since December 2024, C(2026) 5252 Communication plus Annex, published 27 July 2026) IS on that page and is confirmed verbatim. The two section-number claims are true but live on the cra-reporting page ("Section 9.1 of the Commission guidance on the CRA, as well as in Section 5 of the Commission's Frequently Asked Questions on the CRA implementation") and on ENISA FAQ 10, both already in sources. Retrace them.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[43] and [44] (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/881 of 11 December 2025, and its Article 3 four conditions for delaying dissemination).
unsupported.why: Content is correct - I fetched https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R0881 (HTTP 200, 29,368 bytes) and confirmed the title, the 11 December 2025 date, OJ L 2026/881 of 20.4.2026, the ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2026/881/oj printed in the document, the twentieth-day entry into force, and all four Article 3 conditions plus Articles 4 and 5. But that URL is NOT in the 4-slot sources array, and the BRIEF caps sources at 4 while requiring every fact to trace to one. As recorded these two facts are untraceable to a listed source. Note the 11 December 2025 adoption date alone IS in sources: the cra-reporting page says "on 11 December 2025, the Commission adopted a delegated act" and ENISA FAQ 21 says "The European Commission adopted a Delegated Act on 11 December 2025". Only the Article 3 detail in [44] needs the extra slot.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[21]: "Counted on the page: 27 Member States, from Austria to Sweden."
unsupported.why: The count is the researcher's own arithmetic, not a figure ENISA prints. I independently counted 27 country headings and confirm the number, and "Last updated: 10 September 2026" is verbatim on the page. But the fact as written in verified_facts drops the qualifier the researcher put in unverified_or_excluded. It should carry it, and the article must not say every report reaches all 27 - Article 16(2) routes a notification only to the CSIRTs in territories where the manufacturer indicated the product was made available.

unsupported.fact: Verbatim-quote defects that would break any quotation in the copy: facts [4], [18], [25] and [56] carry stray spaces before punctuation ("11 December 2027 , with", "Single Reporting Platform (SRP) . The", "portal.cra-srp.enisa.europa.eu . From there", "telecommunications . The streamlined"); fact [0] joins two separate subparagraphs of Article 71(2) into one sentence; fact [53] renders the title "(EU) 2019/1020" where the OJ body at the cited CELLAR URL reads "(EU) No 2019/1020".
unsupported.why: These are HTML-extraction artifacts, not what the pages say. The substance in every case is confirmed - I re-read all four pages - but a writer treating verbatim_quote as literal would publish text that does not appear in the source. Fact [53]'s title matches the Publications Office record page rather than the URL it cites.

additional_findings: MATERIAL LEGAL GAP, applied inconsistently by the researcher. Article 71(2) carves forward ONLY Article 14 and Chapter IV (Articles 35-51). Articles 15, 16, 17, 24, 64 and 69 are NOT carved forward, so on the face of the text they apply from 11 December 2027. I confirmed Article 64 sits in Chapter VII of the OJ text, not Chapter IV. The researcher applies this caveat rigorously to Articles 13, 24 and 64, and fact [1] correctly states that Article 14 is the only reporting article brought forward - but facts [16], [17], [22], [39], [41], [42], [46], [47], [48] and [50] then present Article 16, 17 and 69(3) duties as operative without the same caveat. The writer must not state that Articles 16 or 17 are in application from 11 September 2026.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE, already in sources but unused: ENISA FAQ 12 states in ENISA's own words that the Article 14 obligations "will apply from 11 September 2026 to all products with digital elements falling within the scope of the CRA, including products that were placed on the market before 11 December 2027." The researcher calls Article 69(3) "the strongest reader hook" and sources it only to the Regulation text; FAQ 12 gives the same point from an agency page already in the list. The Commission summary page says it too: "Reporting obligations apply to all products with digital elements that have been made available on the Union market, including those already placed on the market before 11 December 2027."

SOURCE-URL SWAP STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. sources[3], https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R2847, does not serve the CRA text to any ordinary client: no Accept-Language gives HTTP 400, a browser Accept gives a 2,001,488-byte application/rdf+xml metadata dump. A reader clicking the published source gets an RDF file, not the Regulation. Replace it in the content pack with https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary (Commission, HTTP 200, human-readable, and it independently states the three Article 71(2) dates, the 10 December 2024 entry into force, all four reporting deadlines and the pre-2027 products point) or https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/21b7d4eb-a6e2-11ef-85f0-01aa75ed71a1 (HTTP 200, correct title). Keep the CELLAR endpoint in the research record as the URL the text was actually read from, with the Accept-Language requirement spelled out.

CAVEAT ON THAT SWAP. The cra-summary page carries its own disclaimer: "This summary has been prepared by the Commission services and is not meant to systematically cover the full scope of the Regulation. This summary is not representative of the European Commission's official position." It was last updated 3 December 2025, before launch, and it says "It is also possible for any natural or legal person to notify vulnerabilities, cyber threats, incidents and near misses on a voluntary basis through the CRA Single Reporting Platform" - which ENISA FAQ 27 contradicts for the current release ("The platform has not yet implemented the voluntary reporting functionality provided for under Art. 15(1) and (2)"). The writer must not use that sentence.

UNRECORDED LAUNCH-STATE LIMITATION, same family as the ones the researcher did catch: ENISA FAQ 9 says "No additional corporate entity authentication mechanism is currently used by the SRP." Also unrecorded from FAQ 9: a Secondary AR can access only the notifications they submitted themselves, while the Primary AR can access all of the manufacturer's.

UNRECORDED, useful for the consumer angle: ENISA FAQ 11 says the SRP fields for actively exploited vulnerabilities include the CVE ID and the EUVD ID; FAQ 19 says ENISA "discloses fixed vulnerabilities to the European Vulnerability Database (EUVD)" - an in-sources restatement of Article 17(5). ENISA's careful house phrasing throughout the SRP topic page and FAQ is "manufacturers and, once applicable, open-source software stewards", which is the exact wording the article should mirror.
NO DISQUALIFYING SOURCING. I extracted every URL in the research record: all 16 are on europa.eu domains. No news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet appears anywhere.

NO GUESSED IDENTIFIER, which is notable given the brief's warning. CELEX 32024R2847 and CELEX 32026R0881 are both hyperlinked from the Commission cra-reporting page itself (I extracted href="https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32026R0881" from its HTML), so neither was invented. The cellar UUID came from the redirect chain. All 18 cited ENISA FAQ numbers exist with the titles given - I listed all 31 questions on the page. C(2026) 5252 is printed on the guidance page's downloads block. Article 3 points (1), (14) and (42) are right - I enumerated all 51 definitions. The only constructed URL is the op.europa.eu record page, assembled from the cellar id rather than found on a page; it resolves to the correct document so it is verified, not fabricated, but the record should say it was constructed.

NO DATE CONFLATION ANYWHERE. Adoption (23 October 2024 Strasbourg; 11 December 2025 Brussels), publication (OJ L 2024/2847 of 20.11.2024; OJ L 2026/881 of 20.4.2026), entry into force (twentieth day following publication) and the three application dates are kept separate throughout. Fact [43] is a particular success: Article 14(9) sets a deadline of "By 11 December 2025" and the delegated act is dated exactly 11 December 2025 - a natural place to conflate a deadline with an adoption date, and the researcher did not.

EVERY NUMERIC CLAIM VERIFIED EXACT against the pages: 24 hours, 72 hours, 14 days, one month from the 72-hour notification, the 48hrs counter bug, 1 Primary AR plus up to 20 Secondary ARs, up to 20 notifications before verification becomes mandatory, 27 Member States, support period at least 5 years, security updates available 10 years, ENISA technical report every 24 months, Commission report by 11 September 2028, EUR 15 000 000 / 2,5 %, EUR 10 000 000 / 2 %, EUR 5 000 000 / 1 %, 67 practical examples. The researcher even faithfully reproduced the OJ's own typo "2,5 % of the its total worldwide annual turnover".

TWO SHARP CATCHES I CONFIRM AS CORRECT AND VALUABLE: (a) ENISA FAQ 5 says stewards are covered "to the extent that they are involved in the deployment of products with digital elements", whereas Article 24(3) says "development" - the researcher correctly excluded ENISA's wording in favour of the statute; (b) Article 64(10) grants the microenterprise/small-enterprise and open-source-steward derogation "by way of derogation from paragraphs 3 to 9", while the Article 14 fines sit in paragraph 2 - the researcher flagged the mismatch and told the writer to quote rather than paraphrase. Both verified against the OJ text.

is_vendor_claim FLAGGING IS INCONSISTENT but errs safe. Fact [27] (English only at launch) is flagged as a vendor claim while facts [28] (no API), [29] (no voluntary reporting), [32] (72-hour counter bug) and [58] (resources list) are not, though all are equally ENISA statements about its own platform. No vendor claim is recorded as an independent fact: fact [24] ("initial operating capability") and fact [56] (the Executive Director quote) are both correctly marked and correctly worded as ENISA's own words.

OVERLAP CLAIM VERIFIED: /home/user/travel_scanner/apps/api/app/guides/content/ai-news-eu-transparency-20260802.json exists, news_date 2026-08-02, zh-TW title exactly the one recorded. The researcher's warning also stands: there is no tech vertical index pack in the repo (the only index is ai-news-2026-january-september-index.json) and docs/tech-news-2026/ does not exist, so the first of the two required links cannot be finalised at article level.

My full working record is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-travel-scanner/7f63d65a-c509-5a16-8b56-4ffddc3bb57b/scratchpad/research/tech-news-eu-cra-reporting-20260911-factcheck.json, with the fetched and flattened pages alongside it: celex2847.txt, celex881.txt, ec-cra.txt, ec-sum.txt, ec-guid.txt, enisa-faq.txt, enisa-news.txt, enisa-srp.txt, enisa-csirt.txt.

OVERALL: this is the soundest research record I have checked in this batch. 57 of 61 facts confirmed verbatim at their cited URL, zero refuted numbers, zero fabricated identifiers, zero non-first-party sources. The four fixes are: retrace fact [54]'s section numbers, find a source slot for facts [43]/[44], swap the unusable CELLAR source URL, and add the Article 71(2) caveat to the Article 16/17 facts. Plus delete the now-refuted entry-into-force exclusion and record 10 December 2024 from cra-summary.
